title: Meet Your AI Assistants — Module Quiz

items.q: Skills learned on one assistant transfer to all the others because:
options: Interfaces are legally standardised
They share the same LLM machinery — prediction, context windows, plausibility
They secretly share one model
items.explain: Different wrappers, same engine. That's why this course taught concepts (E1) before tools (E2).

items.q: The four axes where assistants genuinely differ are:
options: Logo, price, fame, and age
Model quality per task, attached tools, limits/pricing, and data handling
Speed, colour scheme, mascot, and country
items.explain: Everything meaningful in tool choice maps to those four; the rest is marketing weather.

items.q: An assistant's cross-chat 'memory' feature works by:
options: Changing how the model fundamentally works
Saving notes and re-inserting them into future context windows
Expanding the model's weights per user
items.explain: A useful trick on top of the same machinery — notes in, notes re-inserted. Worth reviewing what's been saved.

items.q: A long-context assistant quotes 'section 7' of your report. Best practice is:
options: Trust it — long context prevents misquotes
Spot-check the quote against section 7 before using it
Ask it to repeat the quote louder
items.explain: Long-document strength shrinks errors; it doesn't disable them. Quotes and locations are classic verifiable specifics.

items.q: The trade-off of deeply integrated assistants (in your email, docs, OS) is:
options: They cost more electricity
Convenience inside one ecosystem versus freely choosing the best tool per task
They can't write text
items.explain: Integration is real value and real gravity. Let the task choose the tool; let convenience be a factor, not the referee.

items.q: Answer engines like Perplexity are strongest for:
options: Rewriting your notes into emails
Current, factual, source-dependent questions — finding out, not making
Long fiction drafting
items.explain: Search-first design: retrieval then composition with citations. Making and transforming text is chat-assistant territory.

items.q: Five citations arrive with an answer. What verification remains?
options: None — citations settle everything
Confirming key sources actually say what the answer claims
Counting citations across tools
items.explain: Citations prove retrieval, not faithful stitching. The sentence-to-source link is yours to confirm when stakes are real.

items.q: A source-grounded tool (Gemini Notebook-class) asked beyond its sources should ideally:
options: Answer from general knowledge silently
Say the sources don't cover it
Invent a citation that looks right
items.explain: Bounded knowledge is the feature: honest silence beyond the sources is what makes grounded answers trustworthy.

items.q: At work, the FIRST Copilot (or any workplace AI) question is:
options: Which model tier is newest
What has the organisation enabled, and what does policy allow
Whether colleagues think it's cool
items.explain: Workplace AI is governed use — permissions and policy precede capability. E8 turns this into a full habit.

items.q: Paid assistant tiers typically buy these four things:
options: Fame, stickers, priority parking, and hats
Higher usage limits, stronger model tiers, extra features, and data-handling controls
Nothing — paid and free are identical
items.explain: Learn the structure and every pricing page becomes readable — and upgrade decisions become about walls you've actually hit.

items.q: In your personal benchmark, every assistant must get identical task wording because:
options: Vendors require standard tests
Otherwise you're testing your prompting variance, not the tools
Identical wording is faster to type
items.explain: One variable at a time: hold wording constant so differences belong to the tools. E3 varies wording deliberately.

items.q: Your benchmark splits across tools. The professional conclusion is:
options: Re-run until one tool wins everything
Adopt a default plus specialists, noting which task goes where
Abandon AI tools entirely
items.explain: Task-fit beats tool loyalty — the vendor-neutral habit the whole module was building.
